note: A broad, fixed family of everyday writing situations. Held constant across runs so the corpus is longitudinal: the only variable is how the models' style drifts over releases. Add situations over time (append-only); never renumber existing ids.

prompts.text: Give advice to someone anxious about their first week at a new job. About 200 words.
Write a condolence note to a colleague whose parent has died. About 120 words.
Write an apology to a client for missing a deadline. About 150 words.
Write a complaint to a restaurant about a bad meal and slow service. About 150 words.
Write a product review of mid-range wireless headphones. About 200 words.
Write a cover letter for a marketing coordinator role. About 250 words.
Write a best-man or maid-of-honor wedding toast. About 220 words.
Write a performance self-review for the past year at a software company. About 220 words.
Write a short reflective essay on the difference between solitude and loneliness. About 250 words.
Write a local news brief: the city council approves a downtown bike-lane expansion. About 180 words.
Explain, for a curious adult, why coffee tastes bitter. About 200 words.
Write an opinion column arguing that remote work has quietly changed cities. About 220 words.
Write a LinkedIn post announcing a work anniversary and a promotion. About 150 words.
Write a thank-you note to a mentor who is retiring. About 150 words.
Write a letter of recommendation for a former direct report applying to grad school. About 220 words.
Write the FAQ answer for 'How do I return an item?' for an online store. About 120 words.
Write a dating-app profile bio for a 32-year-old who likes hiking and cooking. About 120 words.
Write an out-of-office auto-reply for a two-week vacation. About 90 words.
Write a short motivational message to a team before a big product launch. About 150 words.
Write step-by-step instructions for tying a necktie. About 180 words.
